about: Run 2: a second batch through the same network, fully simulated. With run 1's episodes in memory the worker contacts Corner Mart before Queen St Grocer answers. Every tin is found and fixed or returned, so this recall closes.

recall.hazard: The sounder circuit may fail to activate in an alarm

parties.name: Harbour Market
parties.profile: Fire alarm contractor on Queens Quay by the Toronto waterfront. A crew of four technicians installs and services tins in mid-rise residential buildings. Buys tins from the supplier by the case. The office manager answers the phone during working hours.

parties.name: Queen St Grocer
parties.profile: Fire alarm store on Queen St W in Parkdale, Toronto. A busy contractor with a stock room larger than its jobs need. Installs tins for property managers across the west end and keeps its job sheets on paper.

parties.name: Lakeside Foods
parties.profile: Fire alarm and sprinkler contractor on Lake Shore Blvd W in Mimico, Etobicoke. Pulls recalled stock the same day and ships it back to the supplier with return slips.

directory.name: Corner Mart
directory.profile: Property manager in Parkdale, Toronto, running several mid-rise residential buildings. Buys its fire alarm tins through a local store, not from a distributor. The building manager answers a mobile phone.

initial.say: Delivery note D N five one eight seven seven. Eighteen in stock, twelve sent back.
Ten in stock, fifty shipped back.
Forty in stock, twenty returned, thirty on_shelf at Corner Mart.
We received thirty. The store updated all of them last week: the front says B-4471, the display shows 2.5 and the sounder rings.

expected.note: Hand-computed. mass_balance must equal 180 after every step. Corner Mart' reply must land after Queen St Grocer's claim: until the sender reports the transfer there is no edge to book the receipt against.
